subject: Request: Hosted API SLO relief during launch bump
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@hyperionai.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Hosted API SLO relief during launch bump

Hi Sofia,

Quick note from the Hyperion launch team — we’re seeing a 6x short-term traffic spike after turning on a new pipeline this morning. A few endpoints that hit long sequences (document summarization) are pushing p95 above our expected contract numbers. Our legal/ops folks asked if Redwood can offer a short-term measurement grace while we tune our batching and caching patterns.

Key asks:
- Temporary exception (3-7 days) for p95 breaches tied to this rollout.
- Visibility: a slice of the latency telemetry and any suggested mitigations (sampling, prefix cache hints).
- A written addendum to the SLO that we can share internally — simple and timeboxed.

We’re committed to fixing the client side but need a predictable runway. Happy to jump on a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Priya
Sr. Ops Manager
Hyperion AI

Attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@hyperionai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API SLO relief during launch bump

Hi Priya — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the launch. We can absolutely support a short, well-scoped operational carveout while you stabilize client-side behavior.

Proposal (operations + legal-friendly language):
1) Temporal smoothing for p50/p95: instead of a strict rolling-window percentile we can apply a 1-hour exponential smoothing window for p50 and a 3-hour clipped-window for p95 during the carveout period. This avoids single-minute spikes from failing the entire window.
2) Burst carveout threshold: automatic carveout when regional QPS jumps >350% vs 24-hour baseline for >5 minutes.
3) Sampling & telemetry: we’ll provide a 1% full-trace sample for all long-sequence requests and a high-frequency summary (1m buckets) for the affected endpoints — attached is an example dashboard export.
4) Timebox: proposed 72 hours by default, extendable to 7 days with mutual written approval.
5) Fallbacks & mitigations: we can offer a temporary routing policy that uses a slightly cheaper model variant for >95th-percentile tokens to reduce server-side latency while preserving output quality.

If that sounds workable I’ll loop in legal to draft a short addendum (one page) — attached is a first-pass addendum draft (non-binding). Also copying Marissa to confirm operational feasibility and Ben for commercial alignment.

Next steps: confirm acceptance of the smoothing approach and the default 72-hour window, or suggest edits. We can turn on the carveout same day we’ve signed the addendum.

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142

Attachments:
- evidence_latency_dashboard.png (screenshot of p50/p95 by endpoint)
- proposed_smoothing_addendum_v1.docx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API SLO relief during launch bump (ops feasibility)

SGTM with a couple operational caveats:
- Exponential smoothing will be implemented on the SLO evaluation pipeline (post-hoc). It doesn’t change real-time routing; it only affects whether an SLO violation is recorded in the contract window. Implementation time: ~2 hours to enable the smoothing config and hook up the dashboard slice.
- Sampling: 1% full traces okay, but we’ll also keep an additional high-frequency aggregate for the specific endpoint path (noting sequence length).
- Fallback model variant: we can enable a temporary fallback model that has faster token throughput but slightly lower max-context handling. We need Hyperion ops to confirm that quality tradeoff (we should capture a 50-example prompt set).
- Auditability: we’ll append a short audit log entry for the carveout start/end times and the trigger condition. Legal will want that.

Connor: can you prepare the 50-example prompt capture template and the quality checklist?
Ben: commercial — is a 72-hour default OK, and do we want this covered under an SLA credit cap if things go >7d?

-Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Priya Desai <priya@hyperionai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Hosted API SLO relief during launch bump

Hi Priya — following up with the formal materials attached and a compact summary of the commitments:

Summary (for your internal stakeholders):
- What we’ll change: SLO evaluation will use 1-hour exponential smoothing for p50 and a 3-hour clipped window for p95 for the timeboxed carveout. This only affects contractual violation signaling, not runtime routing.
- Monitoring & evidence: 1% full-trace sampling for affected endpoints + 1m aggregated latency buckets. We’ll share a read-only dashboard link and export (see attached PNG).
- Timebox: 72 hours by default starting when both parties sign the addendum; option to extend to 7 days with mutual written consent.
- Fallback option: temporary model-variant routing for heavy sequences; Hyperion to supply 50 representative prompts within 24 hours for a quick quality run.
- Audit trail & transparency: carveout start/end recorded in audit logs; HubSpot deal note updated (link below).

Action items for Hyperion:
- Reply to this thread confirming acceptance of the smoothing approach and 72-hour default, OR propose a change.
- Send 50 example prompts to connor_obrien@redwood.com within 24 hours if you want us to enable the fallback variant.
- Legal contact for the addendum review (if different from you).

If you’re good, we’ll get the addendum signed and flip the switch the same day.

Thanks — Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
